business_summary.text: Wockhardt is an Indian research-driven pharmaceutical company with a core generics and branded business in India, UK and Ireland, a diabetes biosimilar franchise, and a novel antibiotic portfolio led by Zaynich.

call_points.text: Zaynich addresses a US market of 1.2 million Gram-negative hospital infections across multiple indications including cUTI and cIAI.

history.progress: ₹815.46 Cr utilized out of ₹977.79 Cr net proceeds

deals.progress: ₹815.46 Cr utilized out of ₹977.79 Cr net proceeds

auditor_history.name: M S K C & Associates LLP

guidance.statement: Zaynich peak sales of $1.5-2 bn per year globally
Zaynich business to breakeven in 12-18 months
Normal capex of ₹200-300 Cr over three years, mainly for biologicals capacity
Biosimilar business to double in 24-36 months
Biosimilar capacity to double in 12-15 months
Launch Zaynich in seven to eight emerging markets in 18-24 months

operating_notes.text: QIP net proceeds are ₹977.79 Cr, of which ₹815.46 Cr was utilized by March 31, 2026.
CDSCO approved Zaynich (Zidebactam/Cefepime) for cUTI including pyelonephritis with concurrent Gram-negative bacteremia.
US FDA approved ZAYNICH (cefepime and zidebactam) for adult patients with cUTI including pyelonephritis.
Wockhardt outlined plans to enter 7-8 key emerging markets with high carbapenem resistance in the next 18-24 months.
Zaynich is approved by the US FDA for cUTI, with breakpoints covering almost 95% of carbapenem-resistant cases in the US.
US pricing for new antibiotics is $1,200-1,500 per day for 8-10 days; India prices will be 75-80% below US.
UK subscription model pays a fixed GBP 20 million a year for three years irrespective of supply volume.

holders.name: Tata Mutual Fund - Tata Small Cap Fund
Hsbc Mutual Fund - Hsbc Small Cap Fund

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹965 Cr (+29.9% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹166 Cr (against a loss of ₹25 Cr a year earlier).
Wockhardt reported QIP proceeds utilization of ₹815.46 Cr out of ₹977.79 Cr net proceeds as of March 31, 2026, extending the utilization timeline to FY2028.
ICRA upgraded Wockhardt's credit rating to A- (Stable) from BBB (Positive).
CDSCO granted marketing authorization for Wockhardt's breakthrough antibiotic Zaynich for complicated urinary tract infections.
Wockhardt announced on May 30, 2026, that it received US FDA approval for its novel intravenous antibiotic ZAYNICH for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections.
Wockhardt Limited will hold an Investor Meet on June 4, 2026, at 4:00 PM IST with presentations by Dr. Murtaza Khorakiwala, Ms. Zahabiya Khorakiwala, and Ms. Annapurna Das.
Wockhardt detailed its global commercial launch strategy for its novel antibiotic Zaynich across the US, India, and emerging markets at an investor conference.

On 4 June 2026 Wockhardt told investors it expects $1.5-2 bn peak annual Zaynich sales, with a slight loss in the Zaynich unit for 12-18 months before breakeven, and reported FY26 revenue of ₹3,373 Cr and EBITDA of ₹630 Cr.

watchlist.response: Management declined to give short-term numbers, saying revenue would rise slowly like a hockey stick over 12-18 months.
watchlist.text: Investors asked for revenue projections by segment over six months to two years.

watchlist.response: Management did not give a ROCE figure, saying it had already invested $800 million over 25 years.
watchlist.text: Investors asked for the internal ROCE target.

watchlist.response: Management said Zaynich has a better efficacy and safety profile than cefiderocol and declined to discuss a single molecule further.
watchlist.text: Investors asked how Zaynich peak sales could exceed cefiderocol's ~$250 million.
